RESILIX Customs Defense Desk Synthetic data — demonstration

Ship report · 2026-07-03 · personal / showcase build

A paranoid AI paralegal that shows its work — and refuses to guess.

When an importer discovers years of wrong customs filings, US law offers a powerful escape hatch — the prior disclosure — that is also a trap if filed weak, late, or with a wrong number. The Customs Defense Desk is a working prototype of the tool for that moment: it quarantines every evidence document, decides file-or-refuse in code, computes penalty exposure with every figure bound to a calculation and a primary source, and won't export a thing until a named human approves.

The whole demo runs deterministically with zero API keys — the same case always produces the same packet. The AI seams are deliberately dark: the point is the rails that would make a model safe to add.

The surface

Pick a case. Watch the engine show its work, then hold or file it.

The machinery

Six paranoid choices, each enforced in code

Exhibits are quarantined

Document bodies never cross into the analysis — only enum-typed structured fields do. A booby-trapped invoice can't steer anything, even with an attack the system has never seen.

The disposition is decided by code

File-or-refuse comes from checkable sufficiency predicates over the evidence, never from generated prose.

No number exists without a source

Every figure is computed, cited to statute (19 USC 1592 · CBP ICP · eCFR), and re-scanned at produce time — a packet with an uncited numeral throws instead of existing. The guard once blocked its own author's hand-typed digits.

Estimates are ranges, never "the" penalty

Bounded [min, max] with stated assumptions — false precision in a legal document is the failure mode this exists to avoid.

A deterministic Skeptic re-derives everything

Disposition, figures, deadlines, the rendered text itself — recomputed from raw inputs and compared, ending with a full re-run that must reproduce the outcome byte-for-byte. The maker never grades its own homework.

Export is a locked door

The export function throws unless a named reviewer approved — and it grades the final artifact on the way out. There is no bypass parameter.

The audit

One adversarial cross-model gate, six rounds, closed clean

A different vendor's model reviewed the entire increment read-only and argued until it ran out of objections. Ten findings, all disposed on the record — the argument made the Skeptic and both export doors materially stronger.

RoundWhat it caughtOutcome
R1Skeptic verified only scope figures; guard missed rendered header text; forged approval objects; signed-number and golden-suite gaps; an overbroad legal claim in the docs6 findings — 4 fixed, 2 partially accepted with logged reasons
R2Injected citation refs could launder numbers; prose dates could contradict structured clocks; Unicode minus signs parsed positive3 findings — all fixed
R3–R5Stale-text tamper around the fresh render; value-collision prose; top-level outcome tamperEach fixed; the Skeptic now ends with a whole-outcome deterministic re-derivation
R6—VERDICT: APPROVED

Run it

Two commands, no keys

# local
ENABLE_CUSTOMS_DESK=true npm run dev   # → localhost:3000/customs

# deploy (Vercel free tier)
npx vercel && npx vercel env add ENABLE_CUSTOMS_DESK production && npx vercel --prod

Synthetic data — demonstration. Every case is made up; no real importer's data touches this, and it says so on every screen. Not legal advice: a real customs matter needs a real customs attorney. The flag ships off by default, so a deploy without it is byte-identical to the existing RESILIX ActionOps product.
